identity.title: Geminivirus Betasatellite-Encoded betaC1 Protein Exhibits Novel ATP Hydrolysis Activity That Influences Its DNA-Binding Activity and Viral Pathogenesis.

content.abstract: Plant virus satellites are maintained by their associated helper viruses, and satellites influence viral pathogenesis. Diseases caused by geminivirus-betasatellite complexes can become epidemics and therefore have become a threat to economically important crops across the world. Here, we identified a novel molecular function of the betasatellite-encoded pathogenicity determinant betaC1. The tomato leaf curl Patna betasatellite (ToLCPaB)-encoded betaC1 protein was found to exhibit novel ATPase activity in the presence of the divalent metal ion cofactor MgCl(2). Moreover, ATPase activity was confirmed to be ubiquitously displayed by betaC1 proteins encoded by diverse betasatellites. Mutational and sequence analysis showed that conserved lysine/arginine residues at positions 49/50 and 91 of betaC1 proteins are essential for their ATPase activity. Biochemical studies revealed that the DNA-binding activity of the betaC1 protein was interfered with by the binding of ATP to the protein. Mutating arginine 91 of betaC1 to alanine reduced its DNA-binding activity. The results of docking studies provided evidence for an overlap of the ATP-binding and DNA-binding regions of betaC1 and for the importance of arginine 91 for both ATP-binding and DNA-binding activities. A mutant betasatellite with a specifically betaC1-ATPase dominant negative mutation was found to induce symptoms on Nicotiana benthamiana plants similar to those induced by wild-type betasatellite infection. The ATPase function of betaC1 was found to be negatively associated with geminivirus-betasatellite DNA accumulation, despite the positive influence of this ATPase function on the accumulation of replication-associated protein (Rep) and betaC1 transcripts. IMPORTANCE Most satellites influence the pathogenesis of their helper viruses. Here, we characterized the novel molecular function of betaC1, a nonstructural pathogenicity determinant protein encoded by a betasatellite. We demonstrated the display of ATPase activity by this betaC1 protein. Additionally, we confirmed the ubiquitous display of ATPase activity by betaC1 proteins encoded by diverse betasatellites. The lysine/arginine residues conserved at positions 49 and 91 of betaC1 were found to be crucial for its ATPase function. DNA-binding activity of betaC1 was found to be reduced in the presence of ATP. Inhibition of ATPase activity of betaC1 in the presence of an excess concentration of cold ATP, GTP, CTP, or UTP suggested that the purified betaC1 can also hydrolyze other cellular nucleoside triphosphates (NTPs) besides ATP in vitro. These results established the importance of the ATPase and DNA-binding activities of the betaC1 protein in regulating geminivirus-betasatellite DNA accumulation in the infected plant cell.
